goal: Adds an -ipcconnect option so bitcoin-wallet can connect to a running bitcoin-node over IPC, laying groundwork for online wallet-tool features.

Bundles a large multiprocess/IPC infrastructure update: capnp wrappers for Chain/Wallet/Node/Handler interfaces, a libmultiprocess subtree bump, and assorted build, test, and utility fixes needed to make that work reliably.
reviewability: Stacked on two other open PRs (#10102, #29409); reviewing this PR productively means starting at those first.
Author remains active (rebases through 2026-09) and no mechanical blocker is open, but a design question from April 2026 has gone unanswered.
agreement: Concept support from multiple reviewers over the years including stale approvals (RonSherfey, Korosiua1206).
Unaddressed design objection: combining online/offline behavior in one bitcoin-wallet binary is a potential user footgun, no author reply (ajtowns).
Earlier conceptual worry about coupling wallet tool to the node was raised and satisfactorily answered by the author (jonasschnelli).

categories.name: ipc
why: P2 because it is core plumbing for the long-running process-separation project, adding the Chain/Wallet/Node capnp wrappers and the wallet-to-node IPC connection that #19461 and future online-wallet features build on.
Six years without merging reflects design churn, not urgency, per the rules; the leverage for the multiprocess project remains real.

categories.name: wallet
why: P3 because the wallet-visible change is currently thin: bitcoin-wallet just detects and reports an IPC connection, with no functional payoff yet beyond future potential (RPC-from-tool, sync, shell).
Also reorders the restoreWallet interface signature for IPC compatibility, a mechanical but wallet-facing change.

categories.name: build
why: P2 because it adds real CMake/build-system plumbing for the IPC library and pulls in a libmultiprocess subtree update that fixes actual build failures on macOS, FreeBSD, and sanitizer builds (per the btcsignals commit message).
Also improves libmultiprocess CI reliability (newdeps job, extra warnings), reducing recurring breakage for contributors working on this stack.

categories.name: docs
why: P4 because the documentation changes are small additions (multiprocess.md +6 lines, one line in libraries.md) describing the new option rather than fixing wrong or missing guidance.

categories.name: tests
why: P3 because it extends the functional test framework (combine_logs, per-process log suffixes, longer timeouts) to make multiprocess wallet/node testing possible at all, which unblocks coverage of the IPC feature but is otherwise framework plumbing.

categories.name: tools
why: P3 because it is a genuine addition to the bitcoin-wallet tool's interface (-ipcconnect), but the author states plainly the tool 'doesn't really do anything with its connection to the node yet', so current user value is speculative.

categories.name: utils
why: P2 because the btcsignals commits fix a real correctness/hang hazard (deferred callback destruction blocking bitcoin-node exit and hanging a functional test) and the atomic_load/store fallback fixes real build failures on multiple platforms, independent of the wider IPC feature.

result.summary: This PR adds an -ipcconnect option to the bitcoin-wallet tool (and -ipcbind to bitcoin-node) so the tool can connect to a running node over a unix socket, laying groundwork for future online wallet-tool functionality (sync, serve, shell, RPC pass-through). It is bundled with a very large amount of supporting infrastructure: capnp IPC wrappers for the Chain, Wallet, Node, and Handler interfaces, a libmultiprocess subtree bump with many CI and correctness fixes, build-system wiring, and functional-test-framework changes to support multiple debug logs and slower multiprocess timing. The PR is built on top of two other long-open PRs (#10102, #29409) and is itself a base for #19461.
result.problem: bitcoin-wallet is currently an offline-only tool; there is no way for it to talk to a running node, which blocks planned features like online RPC invocation, wallet sync, or an interactive shell from the tool, and blocks the broader goal of running node/wallet/GUI as separate processes (tracked in #28722).

open_concerns: ajtowns (2026-04-27): questions why online daemon behavior is being overloaded onto the existing bitcoin-wallet CLI tool instead of a new binary, calling it 'more work and a potential footgun for users'; no author reply since, despite subsequent force-pushes.
resolved_concerns: jonasschnelli (2020-12-18) worried bitcoin-wallet's offline-tool identity would be compromised; ryanofsky clarified the IPC connection is fully optional and offline functionality is unaffected, and jonasschnelli did not push back further.
discussion.author_status: active, force-pushed as recently as 2026-09-09 rebasing onto the underlying #10102 stack, but has not responded to ajtowns' naming/design objection from 2026-04-27

However ajtowns' 2026-04-27 comment raises a concrete usability/footgun concern about the chosen approach (overloading bitcoin-wallet rather than a new binary) that remains unanswered.

categories.name: ipc
categories.evidence: Core subject: adds capnp wrappers for Chain/Wallet/Node/Handler interfaces, the -ipcconnect/-ipcbind options, and IPC context/logging plumbing; carries a libmultiprocess subtree bump.
categories.rationale: This is a central deliverable of the process-separation project, providing the wallet-node IPC connection other work (e.g. #19461) is stacked on. It has been open since 2020 but that reflects review/stacking churn, not diminished importance per the priority rules.

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: Adds the -ipcconnect option to bitcoin-wallet.cpp/wallettool, changes the WalletLoader::restoreWallet interface signature, and touches wallet.h/types.h for IPC serialization compatibility.
categories.rationale: Author states 'The bitcoin-wallet tool doesn't really do anything with its connection to the node yet' — the immediate wallet-user value is speculative, though it does lay groundwork for future online tool functionality.

categories.name: build
categories.evidence: Substantial CMakeLists.txt and src/ipc/CMakeLists.txt additions to build the new capnp wrappers, plus a large libmultiprocess subtree sync with CI config and platform fixes.
categories.rationale: The subtree bump commit message states the atomic fallback fix addresses 'build failures on macOS (Xcode 16.2), FreeBSD 15.1, and the MSan/TSan custom libc++ builds in CI,' a real supported-platform breakage fix bundled into this PR's build changes.

categories.name: docs
categories.evidence: Updates doc/multiprocess.md and doc/design/libraries.md to describe the new IPC wallet capability.
categories.rationale: Small, incidental documentation additions (6 and 1 lines) describing the new option; not fixing wrong or missing critical documentation on their own.

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: Adds per-process log suffixes and combine_logs support, adjusts functional test timeouts and assert_debug_log calls for multiprocess wallet runs, and adds btcsignals characterization tests.
categories.rationale: The framework changes (multiprocess-aware debug logs, longer timeouts because 'BlockConnected notifications are a lot slower with the wallet running in separate process') are necessary to make existing functional tests pass under multiprocess and enable future coverage of the IPC feature, but are supporting infrastructure rather than new regression coverage.

categories.name: tools
categories.evidence: bitcoin-wallet.cpp is directly extended with the -ipcconnect option and connection logic (src/init/bitcoin-wallet-ipc.cpp is new).
categories.rationale: Extends a widely used offline tool with new (currently minimal) online capability; the description frames it as foundational for future subcommands rather than delivering user value now.

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: btcsignals.h changes eager callback destruction on disconnect and adds a std::atomic<shared_ptr> fallback; util/result.h changes the default Result constructor.
categories.rationale: The commit message documents a real hang bug: deferred callback destruction 'kept bitcoin-node from exiting and hung interface_gui.py until timeout' in multiprocess GUI builds, fixed by making disconnect() destroy callbacks eagerly, matching boost::signals2 semantics.

categories.name: mempool
categories.evidence: Only adds a comment in block_policy_estimator.h noting to keep the FeeCalculation struct in sync with its capnp mirror; no behavior change.
categories.rationale: Mechanical comment addition only, a side effect of the IPC serialization work elsewhere; not a mempool policy change.

categories.name: p2p
categories.evidence: net.h and net_processing.h only get comments reminding maintainers to sync new fields with the capnp NodeStats/CNodeStateStats mirrors; no p2p behavior change.
categories.rationale: Purely mechanical annotations tied to the IPC serialization layer, not a change to p2p logic.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: bitcoin-cli.cpp's MakeBasicInit call and rpc/request.h get a parameter/comment update purely to follow the InitLogging/log-suffix signature change made for multiprocess logging.
categories.rationale: Call-site update following a signature change elsewhere; no substantive RPC behavior change.

uncertainties: Whether ajtowns' naming/architecture objection (2026-04-27) is intended as blocking or just a strong preference is unclear since the author has not responded.
The true state of #10102 and #29409 (the PRs this is based on) heavily affects how reviewable this PR practically is; their own review states were not provided in detail.

Given the enormous, multi-year rebase history, it's possible some of the diff content (e.g. subtree merge commits) reflects unrelated upstream libmultiprocess work not specific to this PR's stated purpose.
result.card: This PR adds a -ipcconnect option to the bitcoin-wallet CLI tool so it can connect to a running bitcoin-node over IPC, plus a large stack of underlying multiprocess infrastructure (capnp wrappers for Chain/Wallet/Node/Handler, libmultiprocess subtree bump, build and test framework support). It solves the process-separation project's need for wallet-node IPC (tracked in #28722) but the author admits 'the bitcoin-wallet tool doesn't really do anything with its connection to the node yet' — it's foundational rather than immediately useful. Bundled fixes include a real hang bug (deferred callback destruction blocking bitcoin-node exit, per commit message) and cross-platform build failures on macOS/FreeBSD/sanitizer builds. It depends on two other open PRs (#10102, #29409) and is itself a base for #19461. Review has spanned six years with stale approvals from RonSherfey and Korosiua1206, an earlier conceptual objection from jonasschnelli that was resolved, and a still-unanswered design objection from ajtowns (2026-04-27) about overloading online/offline behavior into one CLI tool.
